title: Align-content and align-self
learningObjectives: Explain align-content and align-self and build a responsive layout with it.

understand.concept: align-content controls how multiple flex lines are distributed along the cross axis when there is extra space. align-self overrides the container's align-items value for an individual flex item. align-content has no useful effect when there is only one flex line.
understand.whyItMatters: These properties solve different alignment problems: align-content positions the lines as a group, while align-self changes one item's cross-axis alignment. The container needs wrapping and multiple lines for align-content to matter.
understand.analogy: Align-content arranges rows of items as a group; align-self lets one item choose its own cross-axis position.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual layout follows the flex or grid formatting algorithm.

explain.narrative: The wrapped flex lines are distributed along the cross axis, while the second item overrides its own alignment.

examples.explanation: The wrapped flex lines are distributed along the cross axis, while the second item overrides its own alignment.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered layout demonstrating the lesson concept.

practise.guidedTask: Create a wrapped flex container with two or more lines. Change align-content and then set align-self on one item.
practise.independentTask: Build a small responsive interface using the concept. Test long labels and more than one viewport width.
hints: Inspect the layout overlay in developer tools.

Check for overflow and preserve reading order.
